Split out of SC026/SC027 by the nasal-spirant adjudication; low-vowel branch corrected and rule repositioned by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication. PGmc *-Nx- > long nasalized vowel + *x, with loss of the nasal (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.1 p.55; Ringe vol.1 §3.2.7(ii) pp.149-150). Pan-Germanic: Go. theihan, brahta, thuhta; OHG dihan, brahta, fuht, fust; OE theon, brohte, thuhte, fuht. Distinguished from the Ingvaeonic law by the comparative test: here the nasal is lost in ALL daughters, whereas SC026/SC027 witnesses keep it outside Ingvaeonic (OHG fimf, gans, ander, jugund). Only *a, *i, *u occur (Fulk §4.1). The low-vowel branch now outputs nasalized long *a-ogonek-macron (transducer symbol {*a-tilde}), NOT *o-long: the rounding is the later Anglo-Frisian SC104, and Gothic, North Germanic, Old High German and Old Saxon all keep unrounded a (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). Moved ahead of SC096 and of the daughter-specific NWGmc/PWGmc innovations, so that a pan-Germanic change no longer follows them. Both branches are witnessed: fist *funxstiz > *fuxsti on the high branch, thought *thanxte > *tha-tilde-xte on the low branch; see the generated firing census for the current population.

New rule 2026 from the SC020 three-rule split (Dossier A). Morphological elimination of the nom.sg. marker *-z after stem-final consonant in athematic consonant stems; complete before PWGmc (R/T 2014: 118). Scope pan_pnwgmc with caveat: absolute in WGmc, conditional in NGmc (dossier). Composed at the cascade head, before PWGmcIjContraction, so contraction-created monosyllables (friend *fríundz) never reach it. Reader-facing chapter written (Phase 5): Chapter 2, before SC005. Campbell §407 p.167 treats *w as an ordinary member of this law and R/T p.53 agree that *wj 'too underwent gemination in PWGmc'; R/T p.52 establish *r and *z as its only genuine exceptions. Confidence stays A: the general law is secure, and the dispute is confined to the *w member, which Fulk §4.10 n.1 p.73 rejects. Every selected corpus protoform containing *wj is short-syllabled and so inside the domain; no clean long-syllable *wj negative control is possible, because by Sievers' law a heavy stem takes the *-ij- allomorph (cf. *lḗwijaną, *smérwijaną). column11: Campbell sec.417 p.170: "When a consonant follows, xs > s in OE" (waestm, -waesma, North. sesta), and the change "is found in all West Gmc. languages, and in North Gmc." (ON isl, ON nysa, OS weslon, OS wastum, OS niustan, OHG niusen, OS/OHG lastar < *laxstra-). Brunner sec.221.2 p.184 adds that the following consonant may also be *j (neos(i)an, thisl, waesma, waestm, Nhb. sesta) and that x stays in wrixlan, where the l is vocalic. Bulbring sec.527 p.215: "xs vor Konsonanten in der Regel zu s". R/T pp.157-158 give PGmc *niuhsijana > PWGmc *niusjan > OE neosan, *sehsto > Nhb. sesta, *thihslu > OE thisl, (post-)PWGmc *wahstm > OE waestm, and conclude that *h was lost "possibly variably, possibly only in some dialects, when followed by two or more consonants"; they read it as a shared northern WGmc change but allow that the North Germanic agreement is partly parallel drift. NOT Proto-Germanic: Gothic retains the *h (bi-niuhsjan, saihsta). For fist itself the cognate set is West Germanic only (Kroonen p.160 *funhsti-: OE fyst, OHG fust, G Faust, Du. vuist, MDu. vuust; Orel p.157 *funxwstiz adds OFris fest, OS fust); no Gothic or ON reflex of this lexeme is attested, so the stage is set from *niuhsjan/*sehsto/*thihslu, not from fist.

column11: Thorhallsdottir 1993 ch.5 pp.114-137, acquired and READ DIRECTLY (the committed vision transcript in the reference library), previously known only through Ringe-Taylor vol.2 pp.12,151. She rejects an inherited PIE *w and derives the Old English *w as an inner-Germanic phonetic hiatus glide (p.136, after Bremer 1886:72-73, cf. p.120). TWO MECHANISMS: (i) regular phonological insertion, environment strictly _ *u, i.e. 1sg and 1pl pres.ind. *-u and *-um and the reduplicated-preterite plural *-um, *-uth, *-un (pp.120,126,127), and (ii) analogical generalization of that *w through the whole present paradigm and the pret.ptc., assisted by the preterite stem *seuw(un) and by etymological-*w verbs such as OE flowan (p.127), complete by pre-OE (p.128 n.23, p.136). Old Frisian shares the generalized type, OHG and OS *j is a separate later inner-German event (pp.123,130,134,136) - this directly confirms the anglo_frisian scope. WHAT CAPR EXECUTES IS MECHANISM (ii): the OE citation form is the infinitive *saan, whose following vowel is *a, NOT one of the cells that receives *w phonologically, so the *w of sawan is analogical and the Foma environment (*a _ V) is a citation-form proxy for the generalized outcome, not a reconstruction of the phonological conditioning. NO SPLIT: the phonological rule has no witness in a citation-form corpus and would be a dead rule, and the generalization is analogy rather than a sound law. The 'distinct mechanisms stay distinct' policy is discharged by describing them separately here and in the reader chapter. Confidence raised B to A because the sole stated ground of the B - that the phonological-versus-analogical architecture had not been checked against the specialist source - is now discharged. Residual uncertainty recorded separately, NOT folded into the confidence: the executable environment is a proxy, and SC102 before SC101 remains an assertion from Ringe-Taylor p.151 which Thorhallsdottir nowhere supports (ch.5 never discusses *a-fronting). DEFERRED: the Foma identifier EAFHiatusWInsertion now understates the rule and should be renamed under the behaviour-neutral rename protocol in a separate pass. See governing memo sec.13.4.

column11: Resolved by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication. The former scope tension (R/T pp.150-152 North Sea Germanic vs Fulk §4.11 p.72 Anglo-Frisian) arose from conflating two changes. Old Saxon shares the NASALIZATION of stressed low vowels (R/T §5.1.2 p.142) but not the categorical, systematic ROUNDING: it retains *a-long consistently in the inherited PGmc class and shows variable *a-long/*o-long in the Ingvaeonic class (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). Nasalization is therefore north_sea_germanic and the rounding SC104 is anglo_frisian.

column3: Anglo-Frisian rounding of the long nasalized low vowel
column12: Created by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication, which found that CAPR had telescoped one later change into three earlier rules. Executable {*a-tilde} -> {*o-long}, unconditioned. Confidence A independently of the disputed *e1 reconstruction that feeds SC025: the rounding is evidenced from PGmc *Nx reflexes, from nasal-spirant reflexes, from retained-nasal forms, and by cross-dialect comparison with Gothic, North Germanic, Old High German and Old Saxon a-long (Campbell §119 p.44, §121 p.47, §128 n.1 p.50; Fulk §4.1 p.55, §4.11 p.72; Ringe vol.1 §3.2.7(ii) pp.149-150; R/T §5.1.2 p.142; Brunner §80 Anm.1; Luick §301.1 p.276). Scope anglo_frisian, not north_sea_germanic: Old Saxon shares the nasalization but rounds only variably for the Ingvaeonic class and not at all for the inherited PGmc class. No explicit *i-nasal-long or *u-nasal-long is represented: those develop exactly like oral *i-long and *u-long (Campbell §121 p.47) and no later rule depends on their nasality.

column11: RETRACTED: the previous entry claimed these are historically post-AF-brightening OE diphthong developments executing too early. That was a misidentification. SC030 IS Anglo-Frisian brightening applied to the first element of the diphthong *au (Campbell §132 p.52 lists 'West Gmc. a > OE æ; West Gmc. au > OE æu' as one and the same ordered step; Fulk §4.12 p.73 'This fronting of a applied also to the diphthong au in OE'), so it is contemporaneous with SC043 and not later than it. EAFBrightening was compiled alone and applied to *x*áu*j*ą, *l*áu*b*ą and *s*t*r*áu*j*a, leaving all three unchanged while fronting *d*á*g*a → *d*æ*g*a: every element of EnglishStarConsonant begins with '*', so no clause can find its context inside the digraph {*áu}. SC030 and SC043 are provably non-interacting and their order is free. SC029/SC030 execute immediately after SC004 EAFAiMonophthongization, which reproduces Campbell §132's own steps (2) then (3). No reorder is required and the anticipated SC031-SC034/SC043 corridor problem does not exist.
column12: Adjudicated 2026 (sc029-sc030-awj-resolution-and-au-fronting-adjudication.md): verdict RETAIN, no reorder, no rule change, no output change. The executable rule is correct; the description around it was not. 'Glide formation' was a misnomer twice over, since the change is the undoing of a West Germanic gemination and its effect is to make the glide vocalic. Stage preoe and scope english_specific are confirmed (OHG houwi, gistrouwen and OS hoi point to the unresolved West Germanic stage, R/T p.173). Confidence stays B for a restated reason: that *auj was the pre-OE input is secure, since both camps converge on it, but whether a discrete change occurred holds only on the gemination account, which Fulk §4.10 n.1 p.73 denies and which Luick called 'wahrscheinlich aber nicht strikte zu erweisen'. 2026 follow-up repair (sc010-w-gemination-and-hay-depth-adjudication.md): hay's protoform was corrected from the anachronistic *xáwwją, which encoded a West Germanic geminate in a Proto-Germanic slot, to *xáwją (R/T p.53 PGmc *hawja, cf. Goth. hawi, ON hey), and SC010 gained the *w branch that now supplies the geminate. Both witnesses therefore reach SC029 as *áwwj, and the two singleton branches were removed as unwitnessed; the surviving pair are stress-notation variants, not a historical stress condition. The domain is the *a type only: the *iwj witness hue geminates at SC010 and is correctly not resolved here (Campbell §120.2 p.46). New chronology edge SC010 -> SC029 (feeding). The unstressed branch has no witness. No OE surface output changed.

column12: Adjudicated 2026 (sc029-sc030-awj-resolution-and-au-fronting-adjudication.md): verdict RETAIN, no reorder, no rule change, no output change. Re-identified as Anglo-Frisian brightening applied to the first element of the diphthong. Kept as a row distinct from SC043 because the isoglosses differ: brightening of plain *a is Anglo-Frisian, while brightening of the first element of *au is English only, Old Frisian having monophthongized au to ā (Fulk §4.12 p.73). One process, two historical events; see §7.1 of the memo. Stage preoe and scope english_specific confirmed correct. Confidence raised B to A: existence, domain, stage and scope are each independently secure across Campbell §132 p.52, Fulk §4.12 p.73 and R/T p.172, the scope claim carrying the independent diagnostic of palatalized OE gēac against OFris gāk. The large majority of the witnessed population carries *au inherited straight from Proto-Germanic, so the rule's historical identity is that of the general *au change and must not be read off the two secondary inputs supplied by SC029. The unstressed {*au} branch has no witness. Residual uncertainty concerns where the SC030/SC032 split falls, since Fulk collapses au > ēa into one step while Campbell and R/T give the æu intermediate; that intermediate has documentary support in the early Bede spelling (aeodbald) reported at Fulk §4.12 p.73.
